entries.test: Public documentation of OpenAI's use of artists' and writers' copyrighted work and the permissions obtained would establish whether it used such work without permission.
entries.note: “Snarfs” conveys appropriation without permission in this context.

entries.test: Public lobbying submissions and statements would establish whether Altman requested a wholesale copyright exemption permitting uncompensated use of creators' work and subsequently complained about appropriation of OpenAI's IP.
entries.note: The insults surround a factual claim about public lobbying and complaints. “Free ride” has a plain contextual reading of using work without permission or payment.
He characterizes a hypothetical downfall as ironic; he does not predict that downfall or assert its possibility. The normalization changes that commitment.

The reminder endorses the underlying account of his personal belief. The normalization changes a retrospective statement about last July into a present-tense claim; his actual subjective probability is not publicly verifiable.

entries.test: Public organizational charts, staffing reports, and statements about the reorganization would establish whether xAI largely dismantled its safety operation to accelerate progress.
entries.note: Marcus adopts the reported finding in his own narration and calls it a scoop. The subsequent insider quotation is separate from this extracted assertion.
“Not what the world needs” expresses a judgment of desirability. “The world is harmed” strengthens it into an assertion of actual harm.
